items.title: Preston Jackson Interview, 1973-09-07
items.q: a fella named John Bell, and I think it was this boudreaux and clarinet.

ctx.x: Well, at that time I didn't have to work. I had a great mother, you understand. And my mother was a pretty good business woman, and my father was a brick mason, although, he wasn't allowed, they wouldn't give him a card in Chicago, so he started to, he was a foreman at the IC Roundhouse. See, now, doing this blue blood plague around here, all out the Annunciation Street, he laid bricks all out there, you understand, and they had to put in these concrete instead of the top of the floors and the groves and things…

We had a mouthpiece over here and a cigarette in here. I looked at this guy and said, I wanted to get this guy to play with this cigarette in his mouth on one side and play on the side. And so we had a little march. So finally Grand Marshal came back saying, fellas, when I whistle, I mean for the drum to start plop, plop, plop, plop, plop, plop, plop, and finally in the bass room, jing, with the cymbals, see. And so this little tune, it went like this. I never will forget this. Ta-da-da-da-da-da-da.…
